docs.title: API Documentation
docs.subtitle: Complete reference for the EraseAI REST API
docs.overviewDesc: The EraseAI API lets you programmatically upload datasets, run automated PII/bias/toxicity analysis, download cleaned data, and receive real-time webhook notifications. All endpoints use JSON and require Bearer token authentication.
docs.capUploadDesc: Upload CSV, JSON, or TXT datasets and run automated analysis for PII, toxic content, bias, and duplicates.
docs.capAnalyzeDesc: Retrieve analysis results with version history and download cleaned datasets in multiple modes.
docs.capWebhookDesc: Receive real-time POST notifications when datasets are analyzed, erased, or encounter errors.
docs.authDesc: All API requests require a Bearer token in the Authorization header. API keys are managed from the Developer Dashboard and are tied to your account and plan.
docs.authStep1: Navigate to the Developer Dashboard and generate an API key.
docs.authStep2: Copy the key immediately — it is shown only once.
docs.authStep3: Include the key in every request as: Authorization: Bearer eak_...
docs.authWarning: API keys grant full access to your account's datasets. Never expose keys in client-side code, public repositories, or logs. Rotate keys immediately if compromised.
docs.webhooksDesc: EraseAI sends HTTP POST requests to your registered webhook URL when dataset events occur. Configure webhooks from the Developer Dashboard or the API.
docs.eventAnalyzedDesc: Fired when dataset analysis completes successfully
docs.eventErasedDesc: Fired when data erasure (delete or redact) is applied to a dataset
docs.eventFailedDesc: Fired when a dataset operation encounters an error
docs.retryDesc: Failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times with exponential backoff. Your endpoint must respond with a 2xx status within 10 seconds.
docs.signatureDesc: Each webhook delivery includes headers to verify authenticity. Always validate the X-Webhook-Signature header against your webhook secret to prevent spoofed requests.
docs.sigHeaderSig: HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the request body using your webhook secret
docs.webhookSetupDesc: These session-authenticated endpoints let you register, update, test, and delete webhooks programmatically. They are accessed via the Developer Dashboard API.
docs.securityDesc: Webhook URLs are validated against SSRF attacks — localhost, private IPs, and internal domains are blocked. Always use HTTPS endpoints in production.
docs.rateLimitsDesc: API requests are rate-limited per calendar month based on your plan. Rate limit headers are included in every response.
docs.headerReset: ISO 8601 timestamp when the limit resets
docs.err400: Bad Request — Missing or invalid parameters
docs.err401: Unauthorized — Missing or invalid API key
docs.err403: Forbidden — Plan does not include API access or row limit exceeded
docs.err404: Not Found — Dataset or resource does not exist
docs.err429: Too Many Requests — Monthly rate limit exceeded
docs.err500: Internal Server Error — Unexpected failure, please retry
docs.useCasesDesc: Common integration patterns for the EraseAI API across different workflows.

docs.ucBatchDesc: Upload and analyze multiple datasets programmatically, then download cleaned versions for retraining.

docs.cicdDesc: Upload a dataset, analyze it for issues, gate on high-severity findings, and download the cleaned output — all in a single script.

firewallDocs.title: AI Firewall Documentation
firewallDocs.subtitle: Browser extension & API reference for the EraseAI AI Firewall
firewallDocs.overviewDesc: The EraseAI AI Firewall is a Chrome browser extension that intercepts prompts before they are sent to AI platforms like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Replit. It analyzes text for secrets, PII, proprietary logic, and prompt injection risks — then lets you sanitize or block the submission in real time.
firewallDocs.capInterceptDesc: Intercepts send actions on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Replit before your prompt leaves the browser.
firewallDocs.capAnalyzeDesc: Scores prompts 0–100 for secrets, PII, proprietary logic, and injection risks with categorized issues.
firewallDocs.capSanitizeDesc: Automatically redacts secrets, IPs, passwords, and PII — then replaces the prompt with the cleaned version.
firewallDocs.step1: You type a prompt in any supported AI platform and hit Send.
firewallDocs.step2: The extension intercepts the submission and sends the text to the EraseAI API for analysis.
firewallDocs.step3: A risk overlay appears showing your risk score, detected issues, and suggestions.
firewallDocs.step4: You choose to Cancel, Sanitize & Send (auto-clean), or Send Anyway.
firewallDocs.installDesc: The EraseAI Firewall is a browser extension built on Manifest V3. It supports Chrome, Edge, and Firefox (with compatibility mode). Install it from your browser's extension store with one click — or use the manual install option below.
firewallDocs.storeInstallDesc: Install EraseAI Firewall directly from your browser's extension store. Recommended for most users — automatic updates are handled by the store.
firewallDocs.storeComingSoon: Store listings are pending review. Use the manual install option below until they go live.
firewallDocs.manualInstallHint: Manual install is for developers, early adopters, and air-gapped environments where the public store cannot be used.
firewallDocs.installStep1: Click "Download Extension" above to get the .zip file, then unzip it on your computer.
firewallDocs.installStep2: Open Chrome and navigate to chrome://extensions.
firewallDocs.installStep3: Enable "Developer mode" using the toggle in the top-right corner.
firewallDocs.installStep4: Click "Load unpacked" and select the /extension folder.
firewallDocs.installStep5: Click the extension icon in the toolbar, enter your EraseAI API key (from the Developer Dashboard), and click Save.
firewallDocs.configDesc: The extension uses Chrome Manifest V3 with the following key configuration:
firewallDocs.browserCompatDesc: The extension is built on Manifest V3 and works natively on Chromium-based browsers. Firefox support requires compatibility mode.
firewallDocs.edgeInstallDesc: Edge is Chromium-based and supports Chrome extensions natively. The install process is nearly identical to Chrome:
firewallDocs.edgeStep1: Open Edge and navigate to edge://extensions.
firewallDocs.edgeStep2: Enable "Developer mode" using the toggle in the bottom-left corner.
firewallDocs.edgeStep3: Click "Load unpacked" and select the /extension folder.
firewallDocs.edgeStep4: Click the extension icon in the toolbar, enter your API key, and click Save. Edge may prompt you to allow the extension — click "Allow".
firewallDocs.firefoxInstallDesc: Firefox uses its own extension format (WebExtensions with MV2/MV3 hybrid). The EraseAI extension can be loaded temporarily for development:
firewallDocs.firefoxStep1: Open Firefox and navigate to about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox.
firewallDocs.firefoxStep2: Click "Load Temporary Add-on" and select the manifest.json file inside the /extension folder.
firewallDocs.firefoxStep3: The extension will load but will be removed when Firefox restarts. For permanent installation, the extension must be signed via addons.mozilla.org.
firewallDocs.firefoxStep4: Note: Some Chrome-specific APIs (chrome.sidePanel) are not available in Firefox. Core functionality (interception, analysis, sanitization) works normally.
firewallDocs.firefoxWarning: Firefox temporary extensions are removed on restart. For persistent installation, the extension must be packaged and signed through the Firefox Add-ons Developer Hub. Some MV3 features may require polyfills.
firewallDocs.installWarning: The extension requires an active EraseAI API key to function. Generate one from the Developer Dashboard. Custom API URLs are restricted to *.replit.app domains for security.
firewallDocs.endpointsDesc: The AI Firewall uses the DevMode API endpoints. All requests require Bearer token authentication with an EraseAI API key.
firewallDocs.pingDesc: Lightweight health check to verify API connectivity. Does not count against rate limits.
firewallDocs.analyzeDesc: Analyze text for security and privacy risks. Returns a risk score (0–100), risk level, categorized issues, and actionable suggestions.
firewallDocs.sanitizeDesc: Automatically redact secrets, PII, and sensitive data from text. Returns the sanitized version with a detailed change log.
firewallDocs.historyDesc: Retrieve paginated scan history for the authenticated user, including daily usage counts and rate limit info.
firewallDocs.extensionDesc: The extension is built with Chrome Manifest V3 and consists of three main components that communicate via Chrome's messaging API.
firewallDocs.archContentDesc: Injected into AI platform pages. Detects the platform, hooks send buttons, intercepts submissions, and renders the risk overlay UI.
firewallDocs.archBackgroundDesc: Background script that handles API communication. Receives messages from the content script, calls the EraseAI API, and returns results.
firewallDocs.archPopupDesc: Extension popup for managing API key, toggling the firewall on/off, viewing connection status, and last scan summary.
firewallDocs.messageFlowDesc: The content script communicates with the background service worker via chrome.runtime.sendMessage. The service worker handles all API calls.
firewallDocs.interceptDesc: The content script hooks into platform-specific send buttons and the Enter key. When triggered, it captures the prompt text and routes it through the analysis pipeline.
firewallDocs.overlayDesc: After analysis, the overlay presents three actions to the user:
firewallDocs.actionCancelDesc: Dismiss the overlay and do not send the prompt.
firewallDocs.actionSanitizeDesc: Call the sanitize API, replace the prompt with the cleaned version, then show the changes.
firewallDocs.actionSendDesc: Bypass the firewall and send the original prompt. Labeled as risky for high-risk prompts.
firewallDocs.rateLimitsDesc: The firewall endpoints share rate limits with DevMode. Limits are enforced per user per day.
firewallDocs.freePlanDesc: 10 scans per day across analyze and sanitize endpoints. Resets at midnight UTC.
firewallDocs.paidPlanDesc: Unlimited scans per day on Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Personal plans.
firewallDocs.err400: Missing or empty text field in request body
firewallDocs.err401: No API key or session provided
firewallDocs.err401Key: API key is invalid or has been revoked
firewallDocs.err429: Free plan daily limit of 10 scans exceeded
firewallDocs.err500: Internal server error — retry the request
firewallDocs.maxLengthDesc: 10,000 characters per request. Longer inputs receive a 400 error.
firewallDocs.minLengthDesc: The extension skips analysis for prompts shorter than 3 characters.
firewallDocs.platformsDesc: The extension automatically detects the AI platform based on the page hostname and uses platform-specific selectors to find input fields and send buttons.
firewallDocs.addPlatformDesc: To add support for another AI platform, add a new entry to the PLATFORMS object in content.js with the platform's host patterns, input selectors, and send button selectors.
firewallDocs.addPlatformWarning: After adding a new platform, you must also add its URL pattern to the content_scripts.matches and host_permissions arrays in manifest.json, then reload the extension.
firewallDocs.devModeDesc: Test the analyze and sanitize endpoints interactively with the built-in DevMode scanner.
firewallDocs.upgradeDesc: Upgrade to a paid plan for unlimited firewall scans per day, plus access to all EraseAI features.
firewallDocs.apiKeyDesc: An EraseAI API key is required for all firewall integrations — the browser extension, VS Code hooks, Replit middleware, and Xcode build phases. Generate one from your Developer Dashboard.
firewallDocs.apiKeyStep1: Sign in to EraseAI and navigate to the Developer section from the navigation menu.
firewallDocs.apiKeyStep2: Click "Generate API Key" to create a new key. Your key will start with the prefix eak_.
firewallDocs.apiKeyStep3: Copy the full key immediately — it will only be shown once.
firewallDocs.apiKeyStep4: Store the key securely. Use environment variables (e.g., ERASEAI_API_KEY) instead of hardcoding it in source files.
firewallDocs.apiKeyStep5: Test connectivity by calling the /api/dev/ping endpoint with your key in the Authorization header.
firewallDocs.apiKeyWarning: Never commit API keys to version control. Use environment variables or secret managers. If a key is compromised, revoke it from the Developer Dashboard and generate a new one.
firewallDocs.vscodeDesc: Integrate the EraseAI firewall into your VS Code development workflow. Scan files on save, block risky commits with pre-commit hooks, and run batch analysis from the terminal.
firewallDocs.vscodeSettingsDesc: Add the following to your .vscode/settings.json to configure the EraseAI integration:

firewallDocs.replitDesc: Wrap your AI SDK calls with EraseAI middleware to automatically scan and sanitize prompts before they reach any AI provider. Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, and any LLM API.
firewallDocs.replitMiddlewareDesc: Create a reusable middleware module that scans prompts before sending them to AI providers:
firewallDocs.replitUsageDesc: Use the middleware in your application code to scan prompts before calling the AI provider:
firewallDocs.xcodeDesc: Integrate EraseAI into iOS and macOS projects. Use the Swift SDK for runtime scanning or add a build phase script to block secrets from being committed.
firewallDocs.xcodeSwiftDesc: A native Swift client for the EraseAI firewall API. Supports async/await and Codable responses:
firewallDocs.xcodeBuildPhaseDesc: Add this as a Run Script build phase (Build Phases → New Run Script Phase) to scan Swift files before compilation and block builds containing secrets or PII:
firewallDocs.troubleshootDesc: Common issues and solutions when using the EraseAI AI Firewall.
firewallDocs.troubleA1: Verify your API key is correct and hasn't been revoked. Check that the EraseAI API server is running. Open the extension popup and re-enter your API key. Check the browser console for CORS or network errors.
firewallDocs.troubleA2: Make sure the firewall is toggled ON in the extension popup. Verify you're on a supported platform (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or Replit). Check that content scripts are injected by looking for the EraseAI overlay panel in the page DOM. Try reloading the page.
firewallDocs.troubleA3: Free plan users are limited to 10 scans per day. The counter resets at midnight UTC. Upgrade to a paid plan for unlimited scans, or check your usage with the /api/dev/history endpoint.
firewallDocs.troubleA4: The hook only blocks files that contain danger-level issues (secrets, exposed PII). Check the error output for specific files and issues. You can temporarily skip the hook with git commit --no-verify, but fix the issues before pushing.
firewallDocs.troubleA5: The sanitizer replaces detected secrets and PII with safe placeholders (e.g., [REDACTED], [EMAIL_REMOVED]). Review the changes array in the sanitize response to see exactly what was replaced. If you disagree with a replacement, report it as a false positive.
firewallDocs.scoreExplainDesc: The riskScore field (0–100) represents a safety score — higher values mean the prompt is safer. The score determines the risk level and the extension's behavior:
firewallDocs.scoreDangerDesc: High risk — contains secrets, PII, or critical issues. Extension blocks submission and shows a red overlay.
firewallDocs.scoreCautionDesc: Medium risk — potential issues detected. Extension shows a yellow warning overlay with sanitize option.
firewallDocs.scoreSafeDesc: Low risk — no significant issues found. Extension auto-sends the prompt without interruption.
